svg.text: A plain blank mask. The aura around the head does the face's job.
Working labels, placeholder looks. Status: proposal, pending Legal review.
The four fighters together, showcase size, three-quarter view
Gameplay size: 40 px and 12 px, colour and flat black, each with a civilian
Expression: neutral, taunt, hurt, rage, triumph
In the greybox scene (the repo's own render as the backdrop)
Protagonist (neutral), Anti-hero (rage, mirrored), Empress (taunt, mirrored), Cyborg (neutral). Three-quarter,
mirrored when facing left so the front always faces the camera. Drawn at 72 px, the size of the greybox fighters.
The mask never changes. The aura around the head is the
expression: a calm ring at rest, a lopsided drifting curl
for the taunt, broken arcs for hurt, a spiked flare for
rage, and a fan of rays for triumph.
The aura ring pulses on the beat of the line. A quiet ring
for a soft line, a flare for a shout. The line and the aura
share one envelope. The ring breaks into arcs and the head
drops. The aura grows and gains layers and shapes with each
form, in the fighter's own colour. It is already planned as
No face work at all. The aura is a flat cel-shaded quad or
ring mesh behind the head, driven by an expression uniform.
It shares the planned aura crown and its VFX budget.
It overlaps the aura crown, which is already the wound
readout, so emotion and wear could clash. It also makes
fighters unreadable when the aura is hidden or suppressed
(hiding, cinematics). Aura colours must stay clear of gold
and red for the Anti-hero and Protagonist.
Common rules kept: the value rule, the two-tone edge, the far beacon, calm harmonious colour, and no borrowed look (masks are designed shapes, never grey and round, with no cross-mark or dot eyes).
